articles.headline: Emi Martínez taken to hospital after suffering head injury in Chelsea's win over Everton
articles.description: Emi Martínez suffered a worrying-looking head injury during Chelsea's Premier League win over Everton on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: チェルシーがエヴァートンに勝利、エミ・マルティネスが頭部の負傷で病院へ搬送
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日に行われたプレミアリーグ、チェルシー対エヴァートンの試合中、エミ・マルティネスが懸念される頭部の負傷を負った。
articles.body:
Emi Martínez has been taken to hospital after he suffered a head injury during Chelsea's Premier League match against Everton on Saturday. 

Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso told reporters that the Argentina international was conscious when leaving the stadium and has been taken to hospital for "precautionary tests," adding: "For now, we need to wait."

He added: "It was a concussion, but more than that. I saw just one clip, but we'll have to wait."

Martínez, 34, collided with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite when rushing from his goal to attempt to punch an Everton free kick out of his penalty area in the 67th minute of Saturday's match at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Both players received treatment on the pitch, with the Everton defender recovering quickly. Martínez, however, received extended treatment from the Chelsea physios and paramedics before being stretchered from the field while receiving oxygen. 

He was replaced by 21-year-old substitute goalkeeper Mike Penders in the 75th minute. Eleven minutes of injury time were added on by the officials at the end of the match following the lengthy stoppage in play.

Two goals from Pedro Neto ensured Chelsea took all three points from their trip to Merseyside.

"We are really pleased. Shame for Emi, but we wish you all the best. This win is for him," Neto told TNT Sports.

Everton manager David Moyes said: "I just said to TV, I've not seen the Martínez injury yet, so I hope he's fine. I really do. I couldn't even see from the dugout. It just looked as if it was a sharing ball in between a couple of people. I don't know what else happened."

Chelsea's victory put an end to Everton's unbeaten start to the campaign and saw their defense hold firm for the first time this season.

"I'm really pleased with the performance, with the win, with the clean sheet," Alonso said. "There are many positives to build on from today. We knew it was going to be a hard challenge to win in this stadium, but we did many things to deserve the win. I think we got many things right. We were very professional, very solid, and it's good to have this feeling to win this way.

"We needed to feel like we could win in this way -- being solid, being strong, looking in control and going through difficult moments.

"In the first half, there were moments where there were corners and throw-ins and you need to overcome these moments. It's very hard in the Premier League to have full control of the game but you need to make sure you don't lose your shape or your condition, and today we did that really well."

Information from ESPN's Beth Lindop contributed to this story.

articles.headline: Álex Baena scores late at Espanyol as Atlético maintain pressure on Barça
articles.description: Atlético Madrid substitute Álex Baena scored late to secure a 1-0 LaLiga victory at Espanyol.
articles.headlineJa: アレックス・バエナがエスパニョール戦で終了間際にゴール、アトレティコがバルサへの圧力を維持
articles.descriptionJa: アトレティコ・マドリードの途中出場のアレックス・バエナが、終了間際にゴールを決め、エスパニョール戦でのラ・リーガにおける1-0の勝利を決定づけた。
articles.body:
Atlético Madrid substitute Álex Baena scored late to secure a 1-0 LaLiga victory at Espanyol.

The visitors were relentless in the first half, but it was the hosts who nearly broke the deadlock when Leandro Cabrera caught the crossbar late on.

Atlético replacement Marcos Llorente clipped the bar after the break before fellow substitute Julián Álvarez -- who had just been denied -- teed up Baena for the 89th-minute winner.

There was an early chance for Juventus loanee Jonathan David, who struck just over the crossbar in the sixth minute.

Roberto Fernández tried to nod the hosts in front before David came even closer from the right, but Ángel Fortuño was alert, sticking an arm out to deny the Canada striker.

The hosts' best chance of the first half came late on, when Cabrera rushed forward to meet a loose ball from a cross, bending it towards Jan Oblak, who rose to meet it, but the Uruguayan's effort clipped the bar.

The Espanyol keeper tipped over another late effort from Álvarez, who then earned the assist for the winner from a squared pass to Baena.

Her curled it stylishly into the top corner with one minute remaining in normal time, and a stoppage-time save by Jan Oblak from a Marcos Fernández effort preserved all three points.

articles.headline: Why are Man City fans bringing inflatable bananas to games?
articles.description: Man City fans keep waving hundreds of inflatable bananas, but how do they relate to the club's guilty verdict?
articles.headlineJa: なぜマン・シティのファンは試合に空気入りのバナナを持ってくるのか？
articles.descriptionJa: マン・シティのファンは何百もの空気入りのバナナを振り回しているが、それがクラブの有罪判決とどのように関係しているのか？
articles.body:
Back in Premier League action for the first time since being found guilty of serious financial rules breaches, Manchester City entered the pitch against Liverpool to a predictably hostile reception from the Anfield faithful.

With accusatory banners unfurled, boos audible, and chanting reverberating around the stadium, many of the traveling City fans decided to put on a defiant display of their own with one particular aspect of their matchday counter-protests raising quizzical eyebrows among onlookers -- namely, the large number of inflatable bananas being wielded among the away section.

While looking like an ostensibly odd choice to those unaware, it was not a spur-of-the-moment call -- nor is it a recent phenomenon. In fact, City fans have actually been taking inflatable bananas to games since the 1980s.

Indeed, the practice dates back to the 1987-88 season in particular. Having been demoted down into the English second tier from the old First Division the previous season, it's said that one match-going City fan decided to lighten the atmosphere at Maine Road by taking a large inflatable banana along to a game.

It also happens that the club had a popular striker by the name of Imre Varadi playing for them at the time. Varadi spent two seasons with City during his nomadic career, in which time he acquired the affectionate nickname "Imre Banana" on the terraces. This led to a rise in the number of inflatable bananas showing up in the crowd at Maine Road -- the practice quickly caught on and has endured, if fairly intermittently, for almost 40 years.

Bananas were relatively commonplace at City matches during the 1980s and '90s though the fad did appear to phase out during the modern era, following the club's stadium change and takeover in the mid-2000s. However, last Sunday's heated faceoff with rivals Liverpool saw the trend revived as hundreds of yellow plastic effigies were seen bobbing around in the Anfield Road Stand.

Ahead of City's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town, manager Enzo Maresca said he was looking forward to seeing the stands filled with bananas.

"It's very nice," Maresca told reporters on Friday. "I didn't know the history behind the banana, but I hope tomorrow I can see many bananas in the stadium.

"I think it creates a nice environment for the fans and for everyone that is in the stadium."

So, while City were busy being lambasted as "cheats" from fans around the league and being threatened with potential relegation, their fans were waving bananas around as a slightly eccentric homage to their days in the lower leagues.

articles.headline: Pedro Neto nets brace as Chelsea end Everton's unbeaten run
articles.description: Pedro Neto scored twice in the second half to guide Chelsea to a 2-0 win at Everton on Saturday in a Premier League match marred by a serious-looking head injury to Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martínez.
articles.body:
Pedro Neto scored twice in the second half to guide Chelsea to a 2-0 win at Everton on Saturday in a Premier League match marred by a serious-looking head injury to Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martínez.

Morgan Rogers' eventful afternoon at Everton could have ended with a sending-off before half time but his good fortune was to Chelsea's benefit as the England forward delivered the key moment in a 2-0 victory.

The £117 million summer signing was already on a yellow card for a tussle with James Tarkowski when he went in studs up in a 50-50 with James Garner, catching his opponent high up on his shin.

It was a challenge neither referee Paul Tierney nor VAR felt warranted a second caution or even a straight red much to Everton's frustration and that turned to annoyance when the 24-year-old's driving run to the byline created the breakthrough for Neto 44 seconds after half time.

Rogers' later tumbling in the penalty area after brushing up against Tarkowski only enhanced his role as villain in the eyes of home fans.

When Neto slid home from Jordan Henderson's deflected free-kick for the first Premier League double of his career, the end of Everton's unbeaten start to the season was confirmed even with 11 minutes of added time still remaining.

However, it was not all good news for the visitors as they had goalkeeper Martínez carried off and taken to hospital after a clash of heads with Toffees centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite.

Belgian 21-year-old Mike Penders came on for a 25-minute Premier League debut and had the honour of not only becoming Chelsea's youngest goalkeeper in the competition but also helping secure their first top-flight clean sheet in 23 matches.

The 2-0 scoreline was harsh on the hosts, who were a match for their opponents having come to life midway through the first half when Harrison Armstrong was booked for a strong but fair-looking challenge on Josh Acheampong.

Prior to that Cole Palmer and Henderson had both tested Pickford from distance but conceded better chances as Merlin Röhl's shot saved by Martinez, who then conceded a corner for delaying the restart.

The goalkeeper was forced into a better stop to deny Thierno Barry who had half an empty net to aim at but directed his header straight at the Argentine, who also tipped over a Grealish shot which bounced into the turf and looked like dropping under the crossbar.

By then Rogers and Tarkowski had both been booked after the former responded to being barged to the floor off the ball by grabbing the Everton captain's shirt.

Moisés Caicedo smashed a brilliantly controlled volley against the angle of post and crossbar from Henderson's deep corner before the flashpoint of the game.

Rogers' lunging challenge on Garner left both writhing on the pitch but it was deemed not worthy of further action.

Pickford tipped over a Neto effort while they were still waiting for Garner to be allowed back on after treatment.

articles.headline: Sources: Eagles' Jalen Hurts, out indefinitely with blood clot, not planned for IR
articles.description: The Eagles are not planning to put Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, sources told ESPN, even as he remains sidelined indefinitely with a superficial blood clot.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：イーグルスのジェイレン・ハーツ、血栓により無期限欠場、IR入りは予定せず
articles.descriptionJa: イーグルスは、ジェイレン・ハーツが表在性血栓により無期限の戦線離脱を余儀なくされているものの、彼をIR（負傷者リスト）に登録する予定はないと関係者がESPNに語った。
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are not planning to place quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, sources told ESPN, even as he remains sidelined indefinitely because of a superficial blood clot.

The team, according to sources, has not even discussed the possibility of injured reserve, which would sideline Hurts for a minimum of four weeks.

Hurts and the Eagles are still gathering more information and seeking additional medical opinions, with the quarterback's health the foremost consideration. They believe the blood clot is treatable, with Hurts trying to determine the best course, sources said. The ultimate decision about when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team, and the Eagles are ready to follow his lead. There is still a chance Hurts eventually ends up on injured reserve, if that is the direction the medical information leads them.

In most cases, blood clots are treated with anticoagulants, otherwise known as blood thinners. A player cannot play while on blood thinners.

In general, the minimum timeframe for a moderate dose of anticoagulants is six weeks, sources said. There is a possibility, if the clot is minor enough, that doctors begin with anti-inflammatories only while continuing to monitor. If the clot were to move, as the team said happened in Hurts' case, blood thinners are often the answer. If the clot were to worsen, blood thinners for roughly three months would be the next course of action.

While some around the team might consider Hurts week-to-week, other doctors around the NFL -- who have not examined Hurts -- believe the blood clot could sideline him several weeks. One team's doctor texted ESPN: "It is a broad range and nuance based on size and location and hematology evaluation, but could be six weeks." Another team's doctor had a similar estimation.

The Eagles released a lengthy statement Thursday detailing the process that led to the discovery of the blood clot and Hurts being ruled out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.

While Hurts has been receiving treatment, the Eagles have been working to fortify their roster. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee will start against the Panthers, and rookie QB Cole Payton was promoted to backup. Philadelphia also signed quarterback Joe Milton off Dallas' practice squad. By NFL rules, Milton must be on the Eagles' roster for three weeks.

This is just the latest sequence in what has been a chaotic stretch for the organization that has included hamstring injuries to running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith, the retirement of future Hall of Fame offensive tackle Lane Johnson, and the trade of Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens.

The Eagles believe Barkley returning next week is realistic, but he has been ruled out for Sunday's game.

articles.headline: No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa injures ankle during Wizards' preseason finale
articles.description: First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Wizards' preseason finale after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.
articles.body:
First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Washington Wizards' preseason finale Friday after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.

Wizards coach Brian Keefe told sideline reporter Chase Hughes that Dybantsa had suffered a mild ankle sprain but that the decision to keep him out for the rest of the game was more precautionary.

"We'll look at it more when we get more information," Keefe said.

Dybantsa fell to the ground after landing on his left ankle following a midrange jump shot before limping to the locker room. He had scored 12 points in 15 minutes before his exit in the second quarter.

The Wizards open the regular season Wednesday against the Milwaukee Bucks.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks three underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out three wild-card predictions.

Could the Texans pull off an upset in London? How many sacks will Chiefs defensive tackle Chris Jones have against the Chargers? Could Rams tight end Tyler Higbee be a sneaky play in fantasy? Will Falcons wide receiver Drake London find the end zone for the first time this season? And will Aaron Rodgers move up in the NFL record books against the Bucs? Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

The Packers have allowed the eighth-fewest passing yards per attempt this season, but this matchup presents a much tougher test than the backup quarterbacks they've faced in the past two weeks. The Cowboys convert nearly half their third downs and lead the league in the percentage of possessions producing points. Green Bay can hit big plays, but the Cowboys have enough on offense with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to answer.

New York Giants +1.5 (108 moneyline) vs. New Orleans Saints

On the other side, Saints QB Tyler Shough has struggled even when he has time to throw. So New York doesn't need to constantly pressure him to get stops. That gives the Giants enough to keep this close and win at home.

articles.headline: Source: Patriots likely to activate WR A.J. Brown for Sunday's game vs. Jets
articles.description: Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is likely to be activated after missing the past four games with a right high ankle sprain, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is likely to be activated Saturday after missing the past four games with a right high ankle sprain, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

The Patriots have an open spot on their 53-man roster, and activating Brown adds a premium pass-catching option for quarterback Drake Maye, starting with Sunday's home game against the New York Jets.

In anticipation of Brown's return, Maye compared the situation to basketball.

"I think you see it in the NBA; it's probably the closest thing that I can think of," Maye said earlier this week. "When they start doubling the best player once they get past half court, then they're just leaving a corner 3 open or leaving a guy open for a dunk. So it's kind of like playing receiver with a guy like that.

"We've got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it's going to be tough on defenses. But I know we've got a tough challenge this week, so looking forward to it."

Brown sustained the injury early in the third quarter of the season opener Sept. 9. He returned to practice for the first time Wednesday and said coach Mike Vrabel would ultimately decide when he plays, noting a key consideration would be for the "long haul, not just for temporarily."

Brown was limited throughout the week of practice, according to the Patriots' injury report, and he will likely be eased back into the mix before taking on his usual heavy workload.

The Patriots (3-2), who also have wide receivers Romeo Doubs, Pop Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams on the roster, visit the Chicago Bears on Thursday after Sunday's game against the Jets (2-3).

articles.headline: James, Embiid play 76ers' preseason finale, 'still working on our rhythm'
articles.description: Without VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday night's 125-120 loss to the Celtics, 76ers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what his team may look like this season, including LeBron James and Joel Embiid playing preseason highs in minutes.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- As the 76ers begin a season with a star-laden roster, center Joel Embiid rejects the narrative that anyone needs to sacrifice for this team to succeed.

"I'm against the concept of sacrificing," Embiid said after Friday's preseason finale. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat."

Albeit without second-year starting guard VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday's 125-120 loss to the Boston Celtics for precautionary reasons, Sixers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what his team may look like this season.

The other active Sixers starters -- LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Embiid -- all played preseason highs in minutes and well into the second half. Embiid, who struggled in his last appearance two games ago against the Brooklyn Nets, finishing with six points and eight turnovers, was dominant.​

He scored 27 points, grabbed eight rebounds and added five assists. In the third quarter, he had one of the game's highlights when he threw down an emphatic dunk that drew roars from fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"It's good to dunk. I thought I would never dunk again," Embiid said with a smile. "I guess I don't know what happened. I kind of got possessed."

Still, the group never looked comfortable together on the floor, despite playing against Celtics reserves. After the game, players didn't shy away from their somewhat disjointed performance. Brown pointed to the team's spacing Friday night, which he said led to turnovers, as one of the many things they need to fix moving forward.

"We're not where we want to be yet," he said. "So that's just a part of it. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day."

James echoed Brown's comments, but neither seemed concerned about the Sixers' ability to eventually jell.

"We're getting there," James said. "I mean, obviously we are a couple of weeks in, so we're still working on our rhythm, working on our kinks, and it's not going to be perfect."

The Sixers open the regular season against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Jags unlikely to play 3 international games in 2027 during EverBank renovations
articles.description: Jaguars team president Mark Lamping said the team is unlikely to play three international home games in 2027 while renovations to EverBank Stadium continue.
articles.body:
LONDON -- Jacksonville Jaguars team president Mark Lamping said Saturday the team is unlikely to play three international home games in 2027 while renovations to EverBank Stadium continue.

The Jaguars could play up to three international home games in 2027 as part of the team's agreement with the city of Jacksonville regarding the $1.4 billion renovation of EverBank Stadium. All other home games in 2027 will be played in Orlando's Camping World Stadium while construction on EverBank Stadium continues. The renovated stadium is scheduled to be ready in time for the 2028 season.

"I don't think that that [three international home games] is a highly likely end result," Lamping said. "One of the reasons we wanted to have the ability to play three games in 2027 is at the time we negotiated that, we didn't know whether we were going to be playing in Gainesville or we were going to be playing in Orlando in 2027. So if we were playing in Gainesville, there is the possibility that there could have been some weekends where we couldn't play and we may have had to go play those games elsewhere.

"But the likelihood of three games in 2027, I think it's remote."

Lamping also said it would be natural for the Jaguars to play every home game in 2028 in Jacksonville in the first season in the renovated stadium, which the team has dubbed the Stadium of the Future, but that depends on what the NFL wants.

The Jaguars have two home games in London this season -- a 19-17 victory over Philadelphia at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last Sunday and Sunday's game against Houston at Wembley Stadium -- because of an agreement with the NFL to move an international game they would have been scheduled to play in 2030 to the 2026 season.

Every NFL team is required to give up a home game every four years to be played internationally.

"I think that would be a natural to do [play every home game in Jacksonville in 2028]," Lamping said. "We don't have total control over that because we don't know what's going to happen at the league level. Just because right now every team gives up a home game once every four years, that could change, particularly if there's an advancement to an 18-game schedule. Then that once every four [years] could become more frequently."

The Jaguars have played 15 games in London since 2013 except for 2020 because of the pandemic. Eleven of those games have been at Wembley Stadium and four at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

In 2022 the Jaguars began a three-year contract with the NFL to oversee operations and have full responsibility for -- and get full revenue from -- an annual home game at Wembley, which seats 90,000. Team officials said before that game that they expected ticket revenues to be 40% higher than what it would receive from an annual home game at EverBank Stadium that season.

articles.headline: Ravens believe Browns' Todd Monken wants 'to kick our tail'
articles.description: When Cleveland's coach takes the sideline Sunday, Baltimore players will face off against their fiery former OC.
articles.headlineJa: レイブンズ、ブラウンズのトッド・モンケンは「我々を叩きのめしたい」と考えていると確信
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日にクリーブランドのコーチがサイドラインに立つ際、ボルティモアの選手たちは、かつて自分たちを率いた情熱的な元OCと対峙することになる。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Many in the Baltimore Ravens' locker room believe Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken is not being entirely truthful about Sunday's reunion.

Monken, who was Baltimore's offensive coordinator the previous three seasons, insisted this week that there are no added emotions in facing his former team. But the Ravens feel they know exactly what this game means to the usually fiery Monken.

"If I know Todd the way I think I know Todd, he will want to kick our tail," Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey said.

Despite great success in 2023 and 2024, Monken exited Baltimore nine months ago amid conflicting reports about his relationship with players, especially with quarterback Lamar Jackson, who isn't expected to play Sunday because of an ankle injury. During the 2025 season, when the offense dropped to the middle of the NFL, there were anonymous sources who voiced the players' discontent with Monken's playcalling.

In the offseason, Monken stressed there were no issues between him and Jackson. After Monken was hired by the Browns in January, he received congratulatory texts from Ravens players, including Jackson.

Now, after leading the Browns (3-2) to their best start in five years, Monken is facing the Ravens (4-1) in an early-season battle for first place in the AFC North (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

"He might not say it in the media, but to the team he definitely talks a lot of trash and lets them know [that] he wants to beat us," Ravens running back Derrick Henry said.

During his time in Baltimore, Monken elevated the Ravens' offense to new heights. In 2023, he helped Jackson to his second NFL Most Valuable Player award. The next season, Monken led the Ravens' offense to its first No. 1 ranking in the NFL.

But in 2025, the Ravens unraveled in a disappointing 8-9 season. With Jackson struggling with injuries, Baltimore finished with 311.8 yards per game, which was its fewest in eight years.

Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman said he felt Monken left on good terms, pointing out the impressive production and records set under him.

"When you are a player, you have to make the choice whether you want to make this game about Todd Monken or do you want to make it about going to play football," Bateman said. "I am pretty sure Todd Monken is not worried about Rashod Bateman or what he has done in Baltimore. He is worried about getting the Cleveland Browns right to beat us. So, I think for both sides, the respect is mutual."

Monken feels grateful for how the Ravens handled his final month with the team, and the Ravens can be thankful to Monken for how he helped them land his successor with an influential phone call to Declan Doyle.  

In January, Monken was allowed to work at the Ravens' facility after John Harbaugh was fired as head coach. He had his initial virtual meeting with the Browns while sitting in his Ravens office.

articles.body:
Former No. 1 NBA draft pick Ben Simmons sheds light on his polarizing career in a new ESPN E60 documentary, 'Being Ben.' Now with the Sacramento Kings, the documentary explores the ups and downs of his time in the league and the lifelong passion he has for fishing.

Here's more information about the program.

When does it air?

'Being Ben' premieres on Sunday at 4 p.m. ET on ESPN.

How can fans watch?

Following its linear premiere, 'Being Ben' will stream afterward on the ESPN App. It can be watched on the documentary's streaming hub.
